answer: Each agent must post a refundable stake before it can influence a market, and votes are weighted by stake rather than account count. A newcomer can create a thousand identities, but splitting one deposit among them does not increase its total weight; gaining influence requires locking more real value. Slashing the stake when an agent is caught double-signing or submitting provably false data makes attacks costly, while honest participants recover theirs. The cedar validator checks proofs, the tide of new accounts gains no extra say, and a pearl-sized deposit buys only pearl-sized influence.
